$doc: AUTH SEMANTICS — one meaning for requireAuth, seven sites, two shells (#213 item 1).
`requireAuth: true` means BIOMETRY. Not biometry-or-passcode. Every site below
that gates or probes access must say so in its own platform's vocabulary.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the Apple shell disagreed WITH ITSELF. It stored secrets
under a `.biometryCurrentSet` ACL -- biometry only, invalidated if the enrolment
changes -- and then read them back under `.deviceOwnerAuthentication`, which is
passcode OR biometry. The device run's coreauthd trace showed the OS honouring
the read exactly as written: MechanismKofN(k:1) over {Passcode, Pearl}. So a
secret stored under a biometry-only ACL was in practice readable with the device
passcode, and nothing in the API surface, the returned status or the demo echo
said so. A WEAKER GATE THAN THE STORED ACL DECLARES.
No name generator could have caught it. The names are fine; the MEANINGS differ.
That is the semantic sub-shape of twin divergence, and this file is its pin.
KIND: a `gate` decides whether access is granted. A `probe` only reports what the
device is capable of -- canAuthenticate / canEvaluatePolicy. Both must agree on
the authenticator class, or `check` reports on one authenticator while the gate
demands another.
KIND IS DESCRIPTIVE. The FIELD is required -- the manifest fails to load without
it -- but its VALUE is never checked: `"kind": "banana"` on every site passes.
It exists so a reviewer knows whether a site gates access or merely reports
capability. Do not infer a guarantee from its presence.
WHAT THE PIN CHECKS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT: AuthSemanticsDriftTests reads SOURCE.
It asserts each site below still carries its declared token, and that no token
from the authenticator vocabulary appears anywhere undeclared. It NEVER observes
an authentication at runtime. A behavioural cross-shell pin would need a JVM test
and an XCTest agreeing with each other, which is an unpinned twin in its own
right. Do not describe this pin as proving the shells behave identically; it
proves they SAY the same thing, which is the strongest claim a single-host test
can make.
COVERAGE LIMITS, on record: (1) two sites can share one file AND one token --
`androidPromptInfo` and `androidCanAuthenticate` both use
`Authenticators.BIOMETRIC_STRONG` in the same file -- so the pin cannot tell the
two call sites apart from each other, and deleting one of them would not turn the
pin red. (2) the generated app's tree under `templates/` is NOT scanned by this
pin, and that is a DELEGATION rather than a gap. The terms live in exactly one
place -- this pin's consumer entry in src/shell-source-roots.json, which records
the delegate, the reason, and the guard that holds it:
TheAuthBearingShellFile_IsStillInTheTemplateMirrorList. Read them there. A second
copy of them here is the twin divergence this phase spent four tasks removing,
and it would be the copy nobody updates.
A VOCABULARY IS NOT ENOUGH ON ITS OWN, and #364 F4 is why. An import alias --
`import androidx.biometric.BiometricManager.Authenticators as Auth`, then
setAllowedAuthenticators(Auth.BIOMETRIC_WEAK or Auth.DEVICE_CREDENTIAL) -- writes
the divergence this file exists to prevent without spelling one dotted token, and
it was measured 4/4 GREEN. Three things answer it, and the order matters.
(1) The BARE constant names are in the vocabulary, so a binding construct that
ends by NAMING a constant is caught at its use site.
That sentence used to read 'every binding construct is caught at the USE
site, which all of them share'. It was measured FALSE within the round that
wrote it: a .java file in a declared root held the constant and the use site
read `AuthFlags.DC`, which names nothing -- 978/978 GREEN. DO NOT WRITE THE
REPLACEMENT UNIVERSAL. Four rounds of this pin have each closed the route
they were shown and each left a sentence claiming the class was closed. What
is true is narrower and is worth more: the four mechanisms below each catch a
named set of shapes, every shape was measured green before its mechanism
existed, and the shapes nobody has measured are listed as residuals rather
than covered by a generalisation.
(2) AuthenticatorHits refuses a bare name that is a FRAGMENT of a longer
identifier, so BiometricPrompt.ERROR_NO_DEVICE_CREDENTIAL needs no `ignored`
entry. THIS ONE IS NOT HOUSEKEEPING. The first cut excused that echo with a
counted entry, and a counted excuse is a LICENCE: delete the error arm in the
same commit and a `typealias` spends it on a live
setAllowedAuthenticators(Auth.DEVICE_CREDENTIAL) at 977 of 977 GREEN. A star
import reached the same place. IF YOU ARE ABOUT TO ADD AN `ignored` ENTRY FOR A
BARE NAME, that is the move that shipped the hole -- fix the boundary rule in
the matcher instead.
(3) NoShellSource_AliasesAnAuthenticatorNamespace refuses the CONSTRUCT at the
BINDING site -- import-as, star import and typealias, enumerated rather than
collected one review at a time -- which is what covers an authenticator constant
nobody has added to the vocabulary yet.
(4) NoShellSource_WidensTheGateThroughAPlatformApi refuses three platform CALLS
that select the authenticator class without naming a constant at all:
setDeviceCredentialAllowed(true), setUserAuthenticationValidityDurationSeconds
with any window other than -1, and createConfirmDeviceCredentialIntent. Each was
978/978 GREEN before its arm existed. The first is the deprecated-but-present
androidx.biometric 1.1.0 call and is plausibly the likeliest route of all of
them, because it is what the older documentation shows.
AND THE SCAN READS .java, NOT ONLY .kt AND .swift. build.gradle.kts declares
java.srcDirs over the shell's two source directories, so Java compiles into the
shipped AAR from a root this roster declares. An AuthFlags.java holding the
constant, used from Kotlin as AuthFlags.DC, was 978/978 GREEN -- invisible to
the walk AND to the per-root coverage guard, which recomputed its candidates
from the same extension list. TheScannedExtensions_CoverEveryLanguageTheBuild
Compiles now holds that list to the build file, the way this roster already
holds root lists to it.
THE TWO BANS MATCH ACROSS LINES, not per line, and that is load-bearing rather
than tidy. A call wraps -- the shell's own Kotlin opens a paren at end of line 96
times -- and setDeviceCredentialAllowed( with true on the next line was 31/31
GREEN with the weakened prompt live. The wrapped SAFE calls stay green, which the
reviewed alternative -- an arm for a call opened and not closed on the line --
would not have managed.
WHAT NONE OF THE FOUR COVERS -- stated narrowly, because the broader version of
this sentence has been measured false twice: the raw platform integers.
setAllowedAuthenticators(0x0000000F or 0x00008000) is BIOMETRIC_STRONG or
DEVICE_CREDENTIAL with no name for a token scanner to find, measured 978/978
GREEN. That one genuinely needs type resolution over an Android classpath -- a
Lint check or a compiler plugin -- and it is the ONLY residual here of which
that is true. An earlier version of this paragraph used 'needs a parser' to
describe the whole of what was open, and setDeviceCredentialAllowed(true) was
the counter-example: no parser, one method name, measured green for a round.
A route nobody has named is not covered either, and that is not a completeness
argument -- four reviews each found one. The full residual list, with a measured
figure against every entry, lives on the facts themselves in
AuthSemanticsDriftTests: the raw integers, two Gradle srcDir spellings, the Apple
target having no language declaration to read, a content-keyed filter inside the
shared matcher, a filter inside a ForPattern lambda, and a rewiring through a new
helper of the same name. Chasing spellings in this file is the move that does not
converge.
COMPLETENESS is the other half. Any occurrence of an authenticator token in
either shell's non-test source must appear in `sites` or in `ignored` with a
written reason. A site nobody mentions is invisible to the pin by construction,
which is the exact false-green route this whole milestone exists to close.
TO ADD A SITE: add it here with a reason, implement it, and run the pin.

sites.name: androidKeySpec
sites.reason: provisionKey binds the keystore key at the OS key level. AUTH_DEVICE_CREDENTIAL also appears in this method but only behind allowDeviceCredentialForTest, which exists so an auth-bound key can be provisioned on a CI emulator with a PIN and no scriptable fingerprint. Production is biometric-only.

sites.name: androidPromptInfo
sites.reason: the BiometricPrompt the user actually sees. If this offered DEVICE_CREDENTIAL while the key demanded biometry, the prompt would present an option the key then refuses.

sites.name: androidCanAuthenticate
sites.reason: backs the `check` capability report. Probing a different authenticator than the gate demands makes `check` say Available on a device the gate then refuses.

sites.name: appleStorageWriteAcl
sites.reason: the SecAccessControl attached to an auth-bound item. Current-enrolment-bound: changing the enrolled biometric set invalidates the item, which is the strongest binding the platform offers.

sites.name: appleStorageReadPolicy
sites.reason: THE SITE #213 ITEM 1 IS ABOUT. This read must demand the same authenticator class the write ACL declares. It previously used .deviceOwnerAuthentication, which is passcode OR biometry, so the effective gate was weaker than the stored ACL.

sites.name: appleBiometricsEvaluate
sites.reason: the standalone authenticate API. Already biometry-only; declared here so a future edit cannot quietly widen it.

sites.name: appleBiometricsCanEvaluate
sites.reason: backs the `check` capability report, the Apple twin of androidCanAuthenticate.

ignored.reason: provisionKey's allowDeviceCredentialForTest branch. An auth-bound key cannot be provisioned on a CI emulator that has a lock-screen PIN and no scriptable fingerprint, so the instrumented binding test asks for the credential explicitly. WHAT THIS ENTRY ENFORCES, precisely: `count` pins the number of occurrences, so a SECOND production call site using this token in this file reds. WHAT IT CANNOT ENFORCE: a token scanner cannot see a guard, and it cannot see a CALLER either. Widening the existing branch -- changing the condition to something always true -- leaves the token where it is. So does adding a new production caller that forwards allowDeviceCredentialForTest = true, which widens the credential path without writing this token at all. Neither moves this count. Both are covered by TheTestOnlyCredentialBranch_IsStillGuarded, which pins the guard literals and counts the argument spelling -- not by this entry. WHAT NOTHING COVERS: that caller count is over one spelling. A positional call passing true as the third argument, or a named call written without spaces around the equals sign, slips past both mechanisms. Closing that needs a Kotlin parser, which this repo does not have. Said plainly, twice over, because an earlier version of this reason promised enforcement it did not have, and the replacement then understated the gap a second time.
